gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the battery kits on one basis. EcoFlow STREAM Ultra's 800 W is the most it sends into the home circuit (1,200 W needs the separate STREAM Microinverter), while the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2's 2,000 W is outlet power and it cannot feed the home at all. Their cycle ratings, 6,000 cycles to 70% against 4,000 to 80%, multiply out to about 11,520 kWh against 4,096 kWh of rated lifetime throughput. Notebookcheck measured that about 90% of a STREAM battery's stored energy comes back out at a steady 500 W feed.
standout_why: I compared against balconysolarkits.us/kits (cited), solutionenergy.com/solar/balcony/with-battery (cited), promptquorum.com and our own dealectric.com/balcony-solar-system-with-battery-us. SolutionEnergy already lists the 70% and 80% cycle ratings and says they are not directly comparable. It also gives the STREAM Ultra's 800/1,200 W split. BalconySolarKits already defines output as what the inverter sends to the home. However, SolutionEnergy puts grid feed (STREAM 800 W, Zendure 900 W) and outlet power (C1000 Gen 2 2,000 W, AC180 1,800 W) in one 'AC output / feed-in' column without separating them. No page turns the cycle ratings into a lifetime kWh figure or applies a measured delivered-energy share to the STREAM battery. Our page gives a Notebookcheck usable-energy figure only for the C2000 Gen 2. The wattwattbalcon.fr page would not load because of a TLS error, so I did not compare it. The new part is the arithmetic and the Notebookcheck 90% figure, not the inputs.
decides: This confirms that the pick depends on ChatGPT's closing question rather than reversing it. Only the STREAM Ultra is a true balcony kit that stores power and feeds it into the home circuit. Per the SolutionEnergy and BalconySolarKits figures, its rated lifetime throughput is about 2.8× the C1000 Gen 2's (11,520 vs 4,096 kWh). But its 800 W only offsets household load. It is sold for Utah only, and BalconySolarKits says EcoFlow removed the US store page in October 2026. A shopper who wants to run appliances, or who lives outside an approved state, gets the larger outlet wattage from a power-station kit such as the C1000 Gen 2 or BLUETTI AC180. Those kits give no grid offset and have a lower rated lifetime throughput: about 4,032 kWh for the AC180 by the same arithmetic.

findings.label: Cycle rating (maker basis)
findings.note: Anker's wording: 'After 4,000 cycles, the battery still has at least 80% capacity.'

findings.label: AC output (outlet power, no grid feed)
findings.value: 2,000 W continuous, 3,000 W peak, 120 V 60 Hz
findings.note: This is power at the unit's own outlets. It is not grid-tied, so it does not offset household load the way a balcony inverter does.

findings.label: Max solar input
findings.note: Anker offers 100 W, 200 W and 400 W bifacial panel options. A kit with the 100 W panel uses one-sixth of the 600 W input, so 1,024 Wh ÷ 100 W ≈ 10.2 hours at full rated panel output to fill from empty.

findings.label: AC charging rate (stated two ways)
findings.value: 1,200 W max standard; 1,600 W with UltraFast Charging
findings.note: The same page also lists 1,800 W for AC bypass. Only the 1,600 W figure applies in UltraFast mode.

findings.label: Rated lifetime throughput (derived)
findings.note: 4,000 cycles × 1.024 kWh. This assumes full nominal cycles and ignores capacity fade, so it is an upper bound on the maker's basis.

findings.label: Cycle rating (maker basis as reported)
findings.note: PromptQuorum also states 6,000 cycles to 70%. I could not open EcoFlow's US page (HTTP 429).

findings.label: Battery and grid feed
findings.value: 1.92 kWh LFP (expandable to 11.52 kWh); 800 W to the home standalone, 1,200 W with STREAM Microinverter; 2,000 W solar input (4 × 500 W MPPT)
findings.note: BalconySolarKits gives the same 800/1,200 W split and defines output as what the inverter sends to the home.

findings.label: Rated lifetime throughput (derived)
findings.note: 6,000 × 1.92 kWh. This is not directly comparable with Anker's figure because it is rated to a 70% end point, not 80%. Read it as about 2.8× the C1000 Gen 2's rated throughput on each maker's own terms.

findings.label: US availability
findings.value: Utah only; EcoFlow's US store page removed in October 2026; $1,399 ($1,599 with STREAM Microinverter) on 2026-10-07
findings.source_title: Balcony Solar Kits USA: U.S. Plug-In Solar Kit Tracker (2026)
findings.note: This price is the tracker's dated October figure, not one I checked today. EcoFlow's US store search on 2026-11-15 returned no STREAM listing.

findings.label: Measured energy delivered from battery
findings.value: ≈90% of stored energy at a constant 500 W feed; ≈15% more energy drawn at input than went into the battery when charging
findings.source_title: Notebookcheck: EcoFlow Stream in a practical test
findings.note: Notebookcheck measured the Stream AC Pro (1.92 kWh), not the Ultra, on an EU unit. Applied to a 1.92 kWh battery, that is about 1.73 kWh delivered per full cycle. Carrying it over to the US Ultra is my extrapolation.

findings.label: Cycle rating and outlet power
findings.value: 3,500 cycles to 80%; 1,800 W (2,700 W peak); 1,152 Wh LFP
findings.note: Derived rated throughput: 3,500 × 1.152 kWh ≈ 4,032 kWh to 80%. This is outlet power with no grid feed.

findings.label: Battery and grid feed
findings.value: 3.84 kWh LFP (2 × 1.92 kWh); 900 W microinverter; 2 × 410 W panels included; stops generating in an outage; sold out
findings.note: SolutionEnergy gives no cycle rating, so this kit cannot be normalised against the others.
